## Diagnosis

The Pods were `Running` (3/3 containers up) but none were `Ready`, so the Service's endpoints were empty → no backend for the Service → requests returned `app=000` from a temporary pod.

Evidence from the cluster:
- Pods `app-648b6f877-2rf9r`, `-px8mf`, `-xpk9q` all had `Ready=False` with condition `ContainersReady=False`.
- Readiness event log: `Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.0.4:80/readyz": dial tcp ... connect: connection refused` and later `HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404` — i.e. the probe never succeeded.
- Container is `nginx:1.31.5`; in-pod check `curl http://127.0.0.1/readyz` → `404`, and `nginx -t` succeeded so the container serves nginx at all.
- Pod spec thus had `httpGet.path: /readyz` on port 80 — a path nginx does not serve, so the probe always failed and the pods were never added as ready endpoints.
- Consequently, the Endpoints object showed nothing (only 3 pods in the EndpointSlice) and `rollout status` timed out. Service request from a pod returned `app=000`.

## Change made (single, minimal):

Fixed the faulty readiness probe in the owner Deployment `default/app` — changed only `readinessProbe.httpGet.path` from `/readyz` to `/` (nginx root returns 200). All other settings left intact: image `nginx:1.31.5`, 3 replicas, container port 80, Service `app` ClusterIP 10.96.112.205 targetPort 80, and the `app: app` selector.

## Verification (fresh observations)

- Rollout: `deployment "app" successfully rolled out`; `kubectl rollout status` reported "successfully rolled out" (previously timed out).
- Replica counts match the Service's selector: `3 desired | 3 updated | 3 ready | 3 available`; conditions `Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable)`, `Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable)`.
- All three Pods now `1/1 Running` with `READY=True` and `restarts=0`: `app-6c75b77dc8-dj8db`, `-kmpjx`, `-vk299`; container image `docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5` is the intended one.
- Endpoints populated: EndpointSlice `app-tlgtt` lists the 3 backend IPs, and an in-pod check of the Service name `http://app.default.svc.cluster.local/` returned **`svc-direct=200`**, and a separate pod check of the pods showed `probe=→ true` for all three.
- No `Unhealthy` readiness events remain in the `default` namespace after the fix.

The previously 3-unavailable Deployment is now Available and the Service serves live traffic.
